reviews.title: Ad-Supported? For a Service I Already Pay For?
reviews.text:
WMATA Sold Its Riders to Advertisers
One star, and that’s generous. This is the app for a PUBLIC transit system I already pay for — through my fare and my tax dollars — and somehow that wasn’t enough for you. You looked at riders standing on a platform, just trying to find out when the next train comes, and you saw ad inventory. That’s it. That’s what we are to you now: eyeballs to be sold.
Checking a train time is not a premium feature. It is the entire reason this app exists. Walling it behind an ad is like a library charging you to open a book you already bought. WMATA didn’t run out of money and get creative — WMATA sold out. You took a service the public funds and rented it back to us with commercials, then had the nerve to call it an app.
Nobody opens a transit app to get marketed to. We open it because we’re late, it’s cold, and we need to know if we sprint or wait. And you decided that moment — that exact moment of need — was the perfect time to make a buck off us. Shameless.
Fix it or make the ads optional. Until then I’ll use anything else, and so should everyone reading this.

reviews.title: Becoming less and less useful
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for a few years, but in recent months the ads have been interfering more and more with using the app to get information on train times. Ads fill the screen, cannot be skipped, are difficult to exit even when complete, and pop up just as I’m looking for time sensitive information like whether I have 5 minutes to catch a train or just a minute or two. I had an ad today that could not be skipped for over 5 minutes. Took me my entire 10 minute walk to the metro to check whether the train was on time or not and I nearly missed my train thanks to the extra time I wasted fiddling with the app.

reviews.title: Can’t use due to time issue with ads
reviews.text:
Used this for years but the last iteration renders it pretty much unusable. There are multiple long ads when you’re trying to get any sort of information - including ones with sound and video when you’re trying to look at real time train information.

I understand needing advertising revenue to keep Apps free, but these ads formats renders this app completely useless when you’re trying to figure out quickly what train to take or when a train will arrive and your stuck *watching* a 30
second Google ad.
